exampleAnswers.title: Describing Properties of the Cosine Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\cos{x}?$

  1. The function intersects the $x$-axis at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}.$
  2. The function has a minimum value at $x = 2\pi.$
  3. The function intersects the $y$-axis at $y = 0.$
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\cos{x}.$

Let's go through each statement.

  • Statement I is true. At $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ the function intersects the $x$-axis.

  • Statement II is false. The function has a maximum at $x=2\pi.$

  • Statement III is false. The function intersects the $y$-axis at $y = 1.$

example.title: Describing Properties of the Cosine Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\cos x?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

  1. The function reaches its minimum value at $x = 2n\pi$
  2. The zeros of the function are $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi.$
  3. The range of $y=\cos x$ is $[-1,0].$
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\cos{x}.$

Let's go through each statement.

  • Statement I is false. The function reaches its minimum value at $x = \pi \pm 2\pi, \pi \pm 4\pi, \ldots,$ which can be written as $x =\pi + 2n\pi.$

  • Statement II is true. The zeros occur at $x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots,$ which can be written as $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi.$

  • Statement III is false. The minimum value is $-1$, the maximum value is $1$, and so the range is $[-1,1].$

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\cos x=0$ for $x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},....$
  2. $y=\cos x$ has a minimum value at $x=\dfrac{7\pi}{2}$, which is equal to $-1.$
  3. The range of $y=\cos x$ is $[-1,1].$
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\cos{x}.$

Let's go through each statement.

  • Statement I is true. The zeros of the function $y=\cos x$ occur at $\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi$ for any integer $n.$

  • Statement II is false. $x=\dfrac{7\pi}{2}$ is a zero of the function.

  • Statement III is true. The minimum value is $-1$, the maximum value is $1$, and so the range is $[-1,1].$

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \cos x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for an integer $n$ we have

\[ \cos{x} = \cos{(x+2n\pi)} . \]

Substituting $n=-1$ into the right-hand-side gives

\begin{align*} \cos{x} = \cos{(x-2\pi)} . \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\cos{x} =\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3},$ then $\cos{(x-2\pi)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.$

Finally, then

\begin{align} \sqrt 5\cos(x-2\pi) -2 &= \sqrt 5 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\right) -2 \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\sqrt 5\right)^2}{3} -2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 5 3 -2 \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac {1}{3} . \end{align}

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \cos x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for an integer $n$ we have \[ \cos{x} = \cos(x+2n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=6$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives \begin{align*} \cos{x} = \cos(x+2\cdot 6\cdot\pi) = \cos(x+12\pi). \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\cos{x} = -\dfrac{5}{8},$ then $\cos(x+12\pi) = -\dfrac{5}{8}.$

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Cosine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \cos x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n$ we have

\[ \cos{x} = \cos{(x+2n\pi)} . \]

Substituting $n=-5$ into the right-hand-side gives

\begin{align*} \cos{x} = \cos{(x-10\pi)} . \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\cos{x} = \dfrac 12,$ then $\cos{(x-10\pi)} = \dfrac 12.$

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Evenness Property of the Cosine Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\cos{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\cos{x}$ is $2\pi.$

  • Our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. This means that $\cos{x}$ is an even function, and we have \[ \cos(-x) = \cos{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\cos{x},$ we have \begin{align} \cos(-x+24\pi) &= \cos(-x+2\pi \cdot 12) \\[5pt] &= \cos(-x). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the evenness of $\cos{x},$ we have \begin{align} \cos(-x) &= \cos{x} \\[5pt] &= -1. \end{align}

Therefore, $\cos (-x+24\pi)=-1.$

example.title: Utilizing the Evenness Property of the Cosine Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\cos{x}.$

Notice that our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. If we reflect the graph over the $y$-axis, we get the same picture. This means that $\cos{x}$ is an even function, and we have

\[ \cos(-x) = \cos{x}. \]

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \cos(-a) &= \cos{a} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{3}. \end{align*}
